chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the traveller who prays with the Imam and attains two Rak'at from the Salat. Would that suffice him? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: The traveller (one eligible for shortened prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does a traveller need to add a Rak'at if they join congregational prayer and only catch two Rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific ruling for a traveller who joins the congregational prayer of a resident and catches only two Rak'at, confirming that this suffices for their obligatory prayer without the need to add an extra Rak'at. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the shortening of prayer (Qasr) and the mechanics of joining congregational prayers, emphasizing the Imam's authority in defining the completeness of the act based on the time spent in communion with the Imam. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the interaction between the traveller's reduced obligation and the resident's full prayer structure.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban Bin Usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the traveller who prays Salāt with the prayer leader, and he attains two Rak’at from the Salāt. Would that suffice him from it?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a traveler who performs Salah (prayer) behind an Imam and joins only for two Rak‘at, is it sufficient? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient.’”
